prompt: Count the 1 bits in an int -- including negative values, where the sign bit matters -- and use that count to decide whether a number is a power of two.
explanation: Masking with & 1 asks whether the lowest bit is set, and >>> 1 slides the next bit down into that position; running the pair exactly 32 times covers every bit of an int. The unsigned shift >>> feeds zeros in from the left, so negative values eventually become 0 instead of looping forever the way >> would. A power of two is exactly a number with a single 1 bit, but Integer.MIN_VALUE also has one bit set, which is why the positivity test is not optional.
hints: Loop exactly 32 times: check (value & 1) == 1, then shift value right by one with >>>.
Use >>> rather than >>, or -1 will shift down to -1 forever.
isPowerOfTwo can reuse countSetBits -- but remember Integer.MIN_VALUE has one bit set and still is not a power of two.
